title: $F_X$ is flat over $E_X$
statement:
For finite extensions $E\le F$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside $\Qlb$ and every scheme $X$, the
extension of scalars $F_X\otimes_{E_X}-\colon\Mod_{E_X}\to\Mod_{F_X}$ along
$E_X\to F_X$ ([def-sfb-subfield-coefficient-map], [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars]) preserves
finite limits; that is, $F_X$ is flat over $E_X$.

proof.text: Put $k=\mathbf Q_\ell$ and choose an $E$-basis $b_1,\ldots,b_n$ of $F$. Such a finite basis exists directly from the finite-extension hypotheses: a finite $k$-spanning list of $F$ also spans over $E$; a maximal $E$-linearly independent sublist spans, since any omitted vector outside its span would enlarge it. Write $c:F\xrightarrow{\sim}E^n$ for the $E$-linear coordinate map, so $c^{-1}(a_i)=\sum_i a_i b_i$. Regard $c$ as a $k$-linear equivalence. Both spaces are Hausdorff topological $k$-vector spaces for their norm topologies, addition and scalar multiplication being continuous by the absolute-value inequalities; $F$ is finite-dimensional over $k$. The field $k$ is complete by [def-weil-l-adic-numbers] and nontrivially normed since $|\ell|_\ell=\ell^{-1}\ne1$. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-finite-dimensional-linear-homeomorphism] makes $c$ and $c^{-1}$ continuous. In particular every coordinate $q_i:F\to E$ is continuous. This argument uses completeness of $k$, and does not assume completeness of $\Qlb$.

proof.text:
By [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], on each profinite set $S$ the maps
$$\beta_S:C(S,E)^n\longrightarrow C(S,F),\quad (h_i)\longmapsto\sum_i b_i h_i,\qquad c_S(h)=(q_i\circ h)_i$$
are defined on continuous functions. They are inverse, commute with restriction by precomposition, and are $C(S,E)$-linear. Consequently they define inverse morphisms of condensed $\underline E$-modules, $\underline E^{\,n}\cong\underline F$. The module-morphism equations of [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] hold because both sides are the same pointwise bilinear multiplication maps; the sheaf tensor product in [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor] is the sheafification of the sectionwise tensor, so equality on these bilinear maps is equality of the internal action maps.

source.place: first two sentences: the basis isomorphism on the point

proof.text: Let $P=p_X^*$. The left adjoint and strong monoidal properties in [sk-def-sfb-pullback-from-point] transport the preceding isomorphism to an $E_X$-module isomorphism $E_X^{\,n}\cong F_X$. Here is the finite-sum justification: for its right adjoint $Q$, the adjunction identifies $\operatorname{Hom}(P(A^{\oplus n}),B)$ with $\operatorname{Hom}(A^{\oplus n},Q(B))=\prod_i\operatorname{Hom}(P(A),B)$, and likewise $P(0)=0$. Hence $P$ preserves the finite coproduct and its zero morphisms. The projections characterized by $\pi_i\iota_j=\delta_{ij}$ are therefore preserved too; the diagonal and codiagonal defining addition show that $P$ is additive. Strong monoidality transports each equation expressing $\underline E$-linearity to the corresponding equation over $P(\underline E)$. The ring actions and the inclusion are exactly the transported ones by [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients] and [def-sfb-subfield-coefficient-map]. Write $b_i^X$ and $q_i^X:F_X\to E_X$ for the resulting basis sections and coordinate morphisms; they satisfy $q_i^X(b_j^X)=\delta_{ij}$ and $s=\sum_i b_i^X q_i^X(s)$.

source.place: third sentence: transport by the additive monoidal inverse image from the point

proof.text: Set $R=E_X$ and $B=F_X$. Internal modules in [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] are the ordinary sheaves of modules over these ring sheaves as defined in [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]: an internal action $R\otimes M\to M$, with tensor as in [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor], is precisely a family of bilinear sectionwise maps $R(U)\times M(U)\to M(U)$ compatible with restrictions, and the internal unit and associativity equations are precisely the sectionwise module laws. This follows by the tensor and sheafification universal properties and applies to both $R$ and $B$. We may therefore use [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-limits-sectionwise]: small limits of these modules exist and their underlying groups and actions are computed sectionwise. In particular restriction from $B$ to $R$ takes a limit to the same sectionwise limit with restricted action.

source.place: Tag 03DB, lemma-limits-colimits, limits paragraph; the internal-module identification uses the sheafified tensor definition

proof.text:
Use the coequalizer defining $\operatorname{Ext}(M)=B\otimes_R M$ in [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars]. After restriction to $R$, define natural inverse maps
$$\Phi_M(s\otimes m)=(q_i^X(s)m)_i,\qquad \Psi_M((m_i)_i)=\sum_i b_i^X\otimes m_i.$$
The first formula is $R$-balanced because each $q_i^X$ is $R$-linear, so it factors through the displayed coequalizer; both formulas are morphisms of sheaves by [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor]. Their composites are identities: $q_i^X(b_j^X)=\delta_{ij}$ gives $\Phi_M\Psi_M=1$, and balancing gives
$$\Psi_M\Phi_M(s\otimes m)=\sum_i b_i^X\otimes q_i^X(s)m=\Bigl(\sum_i b_i^Xq_i^X(s)\Bigr)\otimes m=s\otimes m.$$
These equalities on elementary tensors extend by bilinearity and sheafification. For a module morphism $f$, the formula $f(q_i^X(s)m)=q_i^X(s)f(m)$ proves naturality. Thus $\operatorname{Res}\operatorname{Ext}(M)\cong M^n$ naturally as $R$-modules; no $B$-linear structure is asserted on a tuple without transporting the $B$-action.

source.place: last sentence: the explicit natural tensor-with-a-basis isomorphism

proof.text:
Let $D:J\to\operatorname{Mod}_R$ be a finite diagram and $L=\lim_jD_j$. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-limits-sectionwise] and the natural isomorphism in the preceding step, the underlying $R$-module of the canonical comparison
$$\operatorname{Ext}(L)\longrightarrow\lim_j\operatorname{Ext}(D_j)$$
is the comparison $L^n\to\lim_j(D_j^n)$. On sections this is an isomorphism: an $n$-tuple of compatible families $(x_{i,j})_j$ is the same family of $n$-tuples $(x_{i,j})_i$, with the same compatibility equations for every arrow of $J$. The comparison is $B$-linear. Its inverse as an $R$-linear sheaf morphism is also $B$-linear: for the comparison $a$, injectivity of $a$ and $a(b\,a^{-1}(y))=b\,y=a(a^{-1}(b\,y))$ give the required equation. Hence the comparison is an isomorphism in $\operatorname{Mod}_B$. For the empty diagram, both underlying limits are the zero sheaf, which also confirms the terminal-object case. Therefore extension of scalars preserves every finite limit, as claimed.
